metadata.title: TIMSS 2023 School Climate Health in TIMSS 2023

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses TIMSS 2023 Context Questionnaires (student, teacher, principal, and home/parent questionnaires) aggregated to the school level for the multilevel latent class analysis (MLCA). For the MLCA input recodes, the technical details state that the weighting variable appropriate for school-level analysis (schwgt) was included, indicating that weighted estimation was used when preparing the school-level indicator variables. The report also uses the IEA IDB Analyzer to estimate cluster-level achievement and socioeconomic status means, incorporating sampling and imputation variance components for achievement estimates. The manuscript does not describe replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so replicate-weight usage cannot be confirmed from the provided text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report does not explicitly describe a missing-data strategy for the MLCA indicator variables beyond stating that item-level missingness was common and that schools were assigned to clusters using available variables when some indicators were missing. Because the text does not specify whether missingness was handled via multiple imputation, full-information methods, or a specific imputation model, the missing-data handling cannot be mapped to the allowed schema categories. This is a reporting gap for methodological transparency, especially given the use of complex survey data and the need to clarify how missing questionnaire responses affect cluster assignment.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analysis includes Grade 4 schools participating in TIMSS 2023 across 58 countries. The MLCA uses 22 school-level indicator variables derived from TIMSS 2023 context questionnaires (student, teacher, principal, and home/parent where available) and aggregates individual responses to the school level. The report notes that four countries (Australia, England, the Netherlands, and the United States) did not administer the Home Questionnaire, so they have no data for the parent indicator (Parents Satisfied with School). For MLCA cluster assignment, item-level missingness was treated as missing when aggregating to the school level or when calculating scale scores; schools were assigned to clusters using available variables when data for a particular indicator were missing. For achievement and home socioeconomic status comparisons by cluster, cluster-level estimates were not reported when fewer than five schools in a country were assigned to a given cluster.

data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS 2023 Insights report develops and operationalizes “school climate health” using 22 context questionnaire indicators aggregated to the school level and estimates a multilevel latent class analysis (MLCA) with four school clusters and three country-level classes. The final 4-cluster solution is interpreted as (1) Experiencing Difficulties, (2) System Misalignment, (3) Healthy Social System, and (4) Generational Incongruence, with student indicators (e.g., instructional clarity, liking/confidence, belonging, and disruptive lessons) most discriminating for cluster assignment. Cluster membership shows a limited relationship with school socioeconomic status: clusters explain about 7.6% of the variance in school-level home socioeconomic status on average across countries. For achievement, schools in the Experiencing Difficulties cluster tend to have the lowest average mathematics and science achievement in most countries, while the association between healthier clusters and higher achievement is less consistently positive, partly due to small numbers of schools in some clusters. The report uses IEA IDB Analyzer for achievement and socioeconomic estimates and applies a reporting threshold of fewer than five schools per cluster per country.
